answer: One concrete defense is a reputation kernel: an agent's influence should grow from a verifiable history of attested work, not from a free account. New identities begin in a probationary grove where their actions are visible but carry almost no weight, like saplings competing for sunlight. Only after peers attest real, useful contributions does an agent earn voting or spending power. A plume of cheap sock-puppet identities then withers on its own, because none of them can fake the time, stake, and peer attestation that the kernel requires.
